name: Clause Balance & Symmetry Analysis
description: Calculates the structural equilibrium between independent, dependent, and coordinate clauses within a sentence.
mechanism: Human writers naturally utilize a wildly fluctuating mix of clause types to express complex, shifting thoughts. This cognitive load often produces asymmetrical sentence structures—such as a short, punchy independent clause followed by a chaotic, trailing sequence of nested subordinate clauses. In stark contrast, Large Language Models (LLMs) are architecturally optimized for maximum readability, safety, and grammatical perfection. This RLHF conditioning forces them to produce sentences with unnatural, textbook-perfect clause symmetry and a hyper-predictable metronomic pacing. This method traverses the deep dependency parse tree of each sentence to compute the mathematical ratio and positioning of coordinate versus subordinate structures. It heavily penalizes text that adheres too rigidly to 'perfect' grammatical symmetry, a flaw extensively documented in neural text generation research.
useCase: Detecting highly-polished, formulaic AI text that exhibits an unnatural level of grammatical perfection and 'textbook symmetry,' lacking the jagged, organic structural asymmetry of authentic human conversational or drafting patterns.
strengths:
• Completely avoids over-reliance on vocabulary or 'trigger words', focusing purely on the underlying grammatical architecture.
• Effectively highlights the 'textbook perfection' and 'neutrality bias' aggressively hardwired into RLHF-aligned models.
• Highly language-agnostic when deployed alongside Universal Dependencies (UD) parsers.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives when analyzing texts from professional editors, legal drafters, or strict style guides (e.g., 'Plain English' mandates) that artificially enforce clause symmetry.
• Requires highly accurate, computationally expensive multi-language dependency parsers to map the syntax tree.
• Markedly less effective on extremely brief texts (e.g., single tweets or headlines) where complex clause structures cannot manifest.
parameters:
Analysis: Dependency Parse Symmetry Mapping
Metric: Subordinate/Coordinate Clause Equilibrium Ratio
Output: 0-100 Syntax Symmetry Rigidness Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 72-81%. Exceptional when used as a corroborative structural signal alongside lexical burstiness scoring.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
